correctness.rationale: For flag-regular full-dimensional Euclidean P, face-center c_F lies in the relative interior of F-exposing normal cone; regular orthoscheme flag-reflection symmetry forces its ray to the face-center ray. In every characteristic simplex associated to v=edge[v,u] subset faces, v remains nearest and u second-nearest: squared distance differences are affine; at v their gap is edge length squared, at all higher face centers both are minimizing co-nearest. Hence (D2^2-D1^2)/s^2 equals first barycentric coordinate lambda_0 on every simplex. Uniform measure restricts to uniform simplex and lambda_0~Beta(1,d), independent of simplex volume. Boundary sets null. Independently verified exact cube formula Z=1-max/min? Specifically for cube [-1,1]^d Z=min_i |X_i| (nearest two vertices differ by flipping minimum absolute coordinate), with s^2=4, yielding P(Z>t)=(1-t)^d, and bounded Monte Carlo d=2,3,4,6.

originality.rationale: Characteristic orthoschemes and Dirichlet(1,...,1) barycentric law are textbook ingredients, but their combination with Voronoi first/second vertex order gives an all-regular-polytope shape-independent Beta(1,d) invariant. Prior regular-polygon distance papers fix a reference point and random locations, not two closest fixed vertices; regular polytope mean width/Gaussian extrema are different observables. Possible alternative Voronoi margin wording is residual priority risk.
residual_risks: Face-center normal-cone/exposure proof assumes full Euclidean flag-transitive regularity; extension to merely vertex-transitive bodies is unsupported.
Classical Voronoi-margin references under different terminology or an unstated standard consequence of flag orthoschemes may predate this statement.
